subject: general
question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 13 hours, Pipe B can fill the same tank in 26 hours, and Pipe C can fill the same tank in 17 hours. If they are turned on simultaneously, how long will they take to fill the same tank?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity of tank = LCM of time taken by all pipes = LCM(13, 26, 17) = 442 units.

Combined efficiency = (442 ÷ 13) + (442 ÷ 26) + (442 ÷ 17) = 34 + 17 + 26 = 77 units/hr.

Time required = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency = 442 ÷ 77 hours.

442 ÷ 77 = 5 ⁵⁷/₇₇ hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 ⁵⁷/₇₇ hr.**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B, and C = 34 + 17 + 26 = 77 units/hr

⇒ Total time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 442 ÷ 77

⇒ Time taken = 5 ⁵⁷/₇₇ hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 ⁵⁷/₇₇ hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns (Inlet and Outlet)

An inlet pipe adds to the work (positive efficiency), while an outlet pipe or leak subtracts from the work (negative efficiency). Net efficiency = Inlet efficiency − Outlet efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

Calculate the total work done in a cycle of 2 days (or more) and multiply by the maximum possible integer, then calculate the remaining work for the next day individually.
